channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ontario pauses some skills training funding for unemployed people: career colleges
Ford says he feels ‘terrible’ for honest students caught in career college OSAP pause
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Tuesday he feels “terrible” for honest students caught up in a career college system where financial aid is now unavailable, but opposition leaders say the students are only in that situation because of him.

item.title: Former Ontario cabinet minister who resigned over expenses scandal defends promotion
item.description: A former member of Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s cabinet who resigned his post over an expenses scandal is defending his recent promotion.

item.title: Timeline of events in OSAP career colleges warnings, probes
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s government is coming under increasing fire for how it has handled Ontario Student Assistance Program payments at private career colleges.

item.title: Ontario attaches more than 511K people to primary care amid goal of connecting all
item.description: Ontario Health Minister Sylvia Jones says more than 511,000 people have been connected to primary care since her government set a goal of attaching everyone in the province.

item.title: OSAP, affordability questions likely to dominate as Queen's Park resumes sitting
item.description: Provincial politicians are returning to the Ontario legislature Tuesday for the first time in 21 weeks with some new faces thanks to three byelections, a rejigged cabinet and a new cloud of scandal hanging over the government’s head.

item.title: Ontario is planning to launch digital IDs. Here’s what you need to know.
item.description: The Ford government says it plans to launch digital credentials, starting with the Ontario Photo Card and then later expanding to driver’s licences and health cards.

item.title: Ontario to table fall fiscal update next week with 'disciplined' spending approach
item.description: Ontario’s finance minister says he will table his government’s fall economic statement next week, on Oct. 29.

item.title: Ontario career college students worry about impact of OSAP pause, extended to 2027
item.description: Now that the Ontario government has confirmed that a provincewide pause on student financial assistance payments to career colleges will last for months, some students say they’re worried it will prevent them from graduating.

item.title: Ontario minister provides update on OSAP pause
item.description: A pause on student financial assistance payments across all private post-secondary institutions in Ontario will stay in effect until at least the new year, the province’s colleges and universities minister announced Tuesday.

item.title: Ontario to allow over-the-counter hearing aids for sale in the province
item.description: Ontario is planning to make over-the-counter hearing aids available in the province for people with mild hearing loss.

item.title: ‘Sign of respect and solidarity’: Calandra asks Ontario schools, board offices to fly flags to half-mast after CFB Wainwright tragedy
item.description: Ontario’s Minister of Education is asking all schools and board offices in the province to lower their flags to half-mast indefinitely in a show of support for the victims of the Canadian Forces Base Wainwright tragedy.

item.title: This Ontario career college has suspended classes. Here’s why
item.description: An Ontario career college has suspended its academic operations as a result of a province-wide pause on student financial assistance to all private post-secondary institutions.

item.title: Psychotherapist calls for OHIP coverage for mental health services
item.description: A Guelph, Ont. psychotherapist is calling on the Ontario government to expand public health insurance coverage for mental health services.

item.title: National Ballet School, divinity college students among those affected by OSAP pause
item.description: A recent pause on financial assistance payments to private post-secondary institutions in Ontario is affecting divinity schools, Canada’s National Ballet School and many others, with students feeling unfairly swept up in what they describe as a trawling net-like policy.
